title: Closed ambient points with separable field stalks detect an unramified closed subscheme
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be a scheme locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Suppose that for every $y\in Y$ whose image $i(y)$ is a closed point of $X$ [def-weil-closed-points], the canonical residue map $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\kappa(y)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is an isomorphism and $\kappa(y)/k$ is a finite separable algebraic field extension [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Then $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type and unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. In addition, every $y\in Y$ has image a closed point of $X$, the map $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\kappa(y)$ is an isomorphism, and $\kappa(y)/k$ is finite separable. The empty scheme $Y$ is allowed; no quasi-compactness or dimension assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0478 (lemma-locally-finite-type-Jacobson), combined with morphisms.tex Tag 02G7 (lemma-unramified-over-field): closed-specialization and field-stalk argument elaborating the unramifiedness step of curves.tex, lemma-nodal-lci.

proof.text: Choose an affine open cover $U_j=\operatorname{Spec}B_j$ of $X$ with each $B_j$ finitely generated over $k$, as in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. By the affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion], $i^{-1}(U_j)=\operatorname{Spec}(B_j/I_j)$ for an ideal $I_j$. The images of any finite set of $k$-algebra generators of $B_j$ generate $B_j/I_j$. These inverse images cover $Y$, so $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type. No finite subcover is required.

source.place: Tag 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion), affine quotient description, and definition of locally finite type (Tag 01T0).

proof.text: Fix $y\in Y$ and put $Z=\overline{\{i(y)\}}\subset X$. By [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], the ambient closed points in $Z$ are dense in $Z$. Since $i(y)\in Z$, this dense set is nonempty: the closure of the empty set is empty. Choose such a closed point $x\in Z$. The image $i(Y)$ is closed and contains $i(y)$, hence contains $Z$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Thus $x=i(z)$ for a unique $z\in Y$. The homeomorphism onto this closed image identifies $\overline{\{y\}}$ with $Z$, so $z\in\overline{\{y\}}$. In particular $y$ is a generalization of $z$, and the hypothesis of the item applies at $z$.

source.place: Tag 0478 (lemma-locally-finite-type-Jacobson), part (2), applied to the closure of the ambient point.

proof.text: The canonical residue map at $z$ is an isomorphism by hypothesis, so $A=\mathcal O_{Y,z}$ is a field. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism] to $(Y,z)$: the image of $\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ is exactly the set of generalizations of $z$, and its closed point maps to $z$. Since the spectrum of a field has one point [def-weil-affine-spectrum], this image is $\{z\}$. Step 2 therefore gives $y=z$. Consequently every $y\in Y$ maps to a closed point of $X$, and the assumed canonical residue isomorphism and finite separability apply at every $y$.

For every $y\in Y$, the singleton $\{i(y)\}$ is closed in $X$ by step 3. Its inverse image under $i$ is $\{y\}$, since a closed immersion is injective and continuous [def-weil-closed-immersion]; thus $y$ is closed in $Y$ [def-weil-closed-points]. Together with step 1 and the field and separability conclusions of step 3, these are precisely the hypotheses of the reverse implication in [lem-trf-unramified-over-field-local-criterion]. Hence $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is unramified. This proves every assertion. If $Y$ is empty, steps 2 and 3 are vacuous, and the same local criterion applies.
